terms.meaning: A named setting that programs read when they start, such as a database address.
A tool that talks to the app's database and reads its own settings file.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Whole wrapper
sections.what: Loads the local settings file, then the general one, runs the command passed after it, and passes its exit code back.
sections.why: Lets commands that read only the general file also see the local settings.
sections.watch_out: Existing shell variables override the files, which is intended but can surprise someone who expects the file to win.

summary: Runs another command after loading the local and general environment settings files.
purpose: Makes other scripts see the project's settings, since Prisma's command line reads only the general file.
why: Likely reason: the script exists because the database tool does not load the local settings file.
how: Loads the local settings file first, then the general one, so existing values win. Runs the command given after it with the same arguments, then exits with its exit code.
inputs: A command and its arguments on the command line, plus the .env.local and .env files if they exist.
outputs: Whatever the command prints, and an exit code matching that command.
risks: Existing variables in the shell win, so a stale value in the shell overrides the file. If the command cannot start, the script exits with code 1 and prints nothing.
debug: If a setting seems ignored, check whether the shell already sets it. If the command fails silently, run it directly to see its error.
